title: Throttle the anonymous persona-pick logger so a script cannot flood the engagement ledger
detail:
Security meta scan 2026-11-18 (app layer). logPersonaSelection is a public server action with no sign-in (by design: the visitor is anonymous at the persona picker). It wrote one engagement_events row per call with a random idempotency key and had no rate limit, so a loop could fill the table and skew the onboarding persona funnel. The sequence string was stored uncapped.

Fix: a per-IP limit of 30 picks a minute through rateLimitOk('persona-log'), checked before the write and failing open when the limiter is unconfigured, like the other funnel captures (production reports rateLimit: true on /api/status). The sequence label is capped at 64 characters and the personas list at 32 entries before validation.

Same scan, checked and sound: 49 cron routes behind rejectUnauthorizedCron; Stripe, Resend, inbound email, Twilio and FlowWeb webhooks verify signatures on the raw body with constant-time compares; safeNextPath and the hosted-site redirects; pinned-fetch SSRF guard; no secrets in client modules; JsonLd escapes <; check:authz, check:headers, check:security-headers, check:parse-input, check:client-boundary and check:admin-client green.

verify.note: Fails on main: no rate limit, uncapped sequence and personas. Passes when the action limits per IP before writing and caps both.
